Sleep Tracker App / SnoozeFest

TL;DR

The problem

College students aren’t getting enough sleep, which hurts their mental health, social life, and academic standing.

What I did

Analyzed Headspace against 8 usability heuristics, then designed a mobile app from paper sketches through a full style system to a high-fidelity prototype.

The outcome

SnoozeFest: a sleep tracker with a calm, rounded, dreamy visual identity built to make better sleep habits feel approachable.

OVERVIEW

College students are not
getting enough sleep.

Students struggle to juggle freedom and responsibility while keeping a healthy sleep schedule.

That takes a toll on mental health, social interactions, and academic success.

They need a way to improve their sleep habits so they can manage a busy college lifestyle while staying in good mental and academic standing.

My goal

Create an app that lets a user track their sleeping habits and get access to helpful wellness resources.

This project focuses on visual design and interaction design, using those principles to evoke emotion and build a brand.

understanding the space

What do
other apps do?

I benchmarked Headspace, a well-known mental wellness app, against Schneiderman’s 8 Golden Rules of Interface Design and its information architecture, to see what a mature wellness brand does well and where it falls short.

Clear, consistent feedback

Status icons, highlighted nav, and time-of-day suggestions make the app easy to read at a glance. This shaped how I show sleep and activity status in SnoozeFest.

Weak search, some dead ends

Search lacks filtering and assumes prior knowledge, and error states (like a failed sign-up) don’t explain what went wrong. Both became things to avoid.

A calming visual language

Its dark blue base feels calming, with brighter accents for contrast. That color logic became a direct influence on SnoozeFest’s own palette.

INitial protoypes

From paper sketches

to wireframes.

Low- to mid-fidelity

After gathering inspiration from Headspace, I sketched preliminary ideas into 9 screens, including log in and sign up.

Then, I moved into wireframes to work out sizing, spacing, and how elements should be organized on each screen.

  • Sign up / log in

  • Home: greeting, alarm reminder, daily quote, and a prompt to start or end the day

  • Activities: 3 daily curated wellness modules, plus a favorites screen

  • Sleep tracker: most recent sleep overview, quality %, duration, and manual entry

  • Profile: name, synced apps, and activity history

Logo, images, iconography

Nighttime and dreaming were the biggest sources of inspiration for the logo and imagery. Icons, buttons, cards, and input fields all share soft, rounded edges for a cartoonish feel meant to calm and comfort the user.

FINAL SOLUTION

A sleep app that feels as calm
as the habits it's trying to build.

WHAT I BUILT

01

Home page

A personalized greeting, alarm reminder, and a nudge to wind down.

  • User greeting for a sense of personalization

  • Alarm reminder plus notifications on behavior that may affect sleep (screen time, audio, fitness, bedtime, scheduled events)

  • Motivational, sleep-related quote of the day

  • Prompt to wind down with wellness modules

02

Wellness modules

Three daily curated modules that unlock as you complete the prior one.

  • Star button to access favorited content

  • Friendly, cartoonish profile character

  • Tooltip for help or further explanation

03

Sleep Tracker

An overview of last night’s sleep, plus manual entry for non-wearable users.

  • Overview of intended bedtime, actual bedtime, sleep onset, and wake time

  • Data on quality and duration

  • Checked box shows the app is currently synced

  • Manual entry option

04

User profile

Weekly trends and access to past activity, not just raw numbers.

  • Synced apps for automatic, personalized tracking

  • Access to activity history and past modules

  • Progress graph highlighting trend direction over exact numbers

  • “Dream Bigger” section to browse content across all 4 categories

IMPACT & REFLECTION

Learning, growing
& creating something enjoyable.

Most enjoyable part

Building the style guide

Playing with color themes, iconography, and typography led to a dreamy, calm, rounded feel carried through every icon, component, and font.

Happy mistakes?

How is this specific to college students?

In its current state, it isn't. This app has the potential to serve a wider variety of users than my initial intended user group. ->

next steps

Expand campus resources

To tailor towards college students specifically, I want to add a feature that connects users to information and resources available on their own campus.
